adjudication_records.issue_text: Permission gate uses && between isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner so only users who are both admin and owner pass, blocking team admins who should be able to manage the booking (should be ||)

Duplicate guest filtering uses case-sensitive email comparison while the blacklist comparison is lowercased, allowing case-variant duplicates to create duplicate attendee rows and send duplicate invites

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, duplicate filtering is done with a case-sensitive comparison (`!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)`), and blacklist entries are lowercased while the incoming `guest` is not (`blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`). This allows case-variant duplicates (e.g., `A@x.com` vs `a@x.com`) to pass `uniqueGuests`, leading to duplicate attendee rows via `createMany` and potentially duplicate calendar/email notifications. The client-side `Set` uniqueness check in `AddGuestsDialog` is also case-sensitive, so it won’t prevent this either.

adjudication_records.issue_text: catch block for AddGuestsEmails discards the error object via console.log without the error, so email-send failures are silently reported as success with no diagnostic trail

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the email-sending is wrapped in `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(...) } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }`, which swallows the exception and does not log/include `err`. The handler then returns `{ message: "Guests added" }` regardless, so the client will treat the mutation as success even when email dispatch fails, with minimal diagnostics in logs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:44-46 uses && instead of || for the team admin/owner permission check, requiring user to be both admin and owner so team admins get FORBIDDEN

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the permission flag is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, which requires the user to be both a team admin and team owner. Given the variable name `isTeamAdminOrOwner` and subsequent check `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw FORBIDDEN`, this would incorrectly deny access to users who are only admins (or only owners). Using `||` would match the intended semantics implied by the name.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:66-68 duplicate-email check is case-sensitive (guest === attendee.email), allowing re-adding existing attendees by changing email case

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the de-duplication filter compares emails with strict equality (`guest === attendee.email`) and the blacklist check uses `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` without normalizing case. Since neither `guest` nor `attendee.email` are lowercased, an existing attendee email like `User@x.com` can be re-added as `user@x.com`, bypassing the duplicate check shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:141-149 swallows all email errors with bare console.log, discarding the error object and leaving guests silently un-notified with success returned

adjudication_records.issue_text: No upper bound on number of guests in the mutation, enabling a spam/DoS vector with thousands of emails and calendar-API updates

adjudication.rationale: The new TRPC input schema `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` accepts `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.max(...)` (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts). The handler then does potentially expensive work proportional to that array size: `createMany` attendee rows, builds `attendeesList` with `Promise.all`, calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` (calendar API updates), and sends emails via `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` using `Promise.all` over attendees (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts and packages/emails/email-manager.ts). With no upper bound, a client could submit thousands of emails, creating a plausible DoS/spam vector grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Authorization check uses && instead of || when composing isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner, so admins who aren't owners get FORBIDDEN

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, despite the name implying an OR check. This requires a user to be both team admin and team owner to pass the team-based authorization path, so a team admin who is not the owner will fail `isTeamAdminOrOwner` and can hit the `FORBIDDEN` branch (`if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee)`). This matches the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email fan-out uses raw guests input instead of uniqueGuests, sending full AttendeeScheduledEmails to blacklisted and duplicate addresses

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the DB write correctly filters to `uniqueGuests` (excludes existing attendees and `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS`), but the email fan-out calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` using the raw input array instead of `uniqueGuests`. In `sendAddGuestsEmails`, the `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` check determines who receives a full `AttendeeScheduledEmail` vs `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`, so including already-existing attendee emails in the input will incorrectly classify them as “new” and send them the wrong email type. However, the claim about sending emails to blacklisted addresses is not supported by the diff because only `calendarEvent.attendees` are iterated, and blacklisted emails are not added to attendees.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:49-56 — `findFirstOrThrow` with `booking.userId || 0` throws unhandled Prisma P2025 for bookings with null userId, returning a raw 500 instead of a TRPCError

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the organizer lookup uses `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })`. If `booking.userId` is `null`/`undefined` (which the `|| 0` suggests is possible), this becomes `id: 0` and `findFirstOrThrow` will throw when no user exists. There is no surrounding `try/catch` converting that to a `TRPCError`, so the error would bubble up as an unhandled server error rather than a controlled TRPC response.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:116-128 — EventManager constructed with caller's credentials instead of booking organizer's credentials, so calendar updates silently fail when a non-organizer adds guests, causing split state between DB and calendar

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the calendar update is performed via `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...(await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user))] })` (around lines 150-160 in the new file), where `user`/`ctx.user` is the *caller* of the mutation, not necessarily the booking organizer. However, the booking/calendar context (`booking`, `booking.user`, `booking.destinationCalendar`, organizer info fetched separately) indicates the event belongs to the booking organizer’s calendar. If a team admin/attendee (allowed by the permission checks) adds guests, the handler will attempt `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` using the caller’s credentials rather than the organizer’s, which can prevent updating the organizer’s external calendar and leave DB attendees updated but calendar attendees unchanged.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:130-138 — attendees write and updateCalendarAttendees are not in one error boundary; if updateCalendarAttendees throws, committed attendee rows persist with no rollback and retry hits duplicate-attendee path

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the DB write happens first via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` and only afterwards the external side-effect `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` is executed. There is no transaction/rollback around these steps. If `updateCalendarAttendees` throws, the newly created attendee rows remain committed. On retry, `uniqueGuests` filters out emails already present in `booking.attendees` (or in the updated booking on subsequent reads), which can lead to `uniqueGuests.length === 0` and a `BAD_REQUEST` (`emails_must_be_unique_valid`), effectively preventing recovery. This is a real consistency bug exposed by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: email-manager.ts:534-540 — `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` compares against raw guests input instead of persisted uniqueGuests, and case differences cause an existing attendee to receive the wrong 'you're booked' email
matched_golden_ids: The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point to the same core bug: when iterating over the full persisted attendee list, the code decides which email to send by checking `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` (raw input guests) rather than the correct/persisted set (e.g., unique/persisted guests). This mismatch can cause existing attendees to be misclassified and receive the wrong email; the candidate additionally notes case-sensitivity as a contributing factor but aligns with the golden issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: organizer-add-guests-email.ts:31 — subject built from `this.calEvent.attendees[0].name` which after createMany can be a newly added guest with empty name, producing malformed subject like 'Guests Added:  with  at …'

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts`, the email subject uses `name: this.calEvent.attendees[0].name`. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, newly added guests are created with `name: ""` (`guestsFullDetails`), and the `CalendarEvent` attendees list is built directly from `bookingAttendees.attendees` without any ordering guarantee. This means `attendees[0]` can be a newly added guest with an empty name, producing a malformed subject like `Guests Added: <eventType> with  at <date>`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:41-76 — adding guests to a seatsPerTimeSlot booking bypasses the seat-count invariant; no check that attendees.length + guests.length <= seatsPerTimeSlot, allowing overbooked seat events without payment bookkeeping updates

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the mutation unconditionally appends new attendees via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` after only filtering duplicates/blacklist (`uniqueGuests`). There is no check against `booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot` or current `booking.attendees.length` before creating new attendees. Since the handler also includes `seatsPerTimeSlot`/`seatsShowAttendees` in the `CalendarEvent` it builds, this code path clearly applies to seat-based bookings but does not enforce any seat limit, so it can overfill a seats-per-time-slot event.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:49-51 uses && instead of || for isTeamAdminOrOwner, so team admins who are not owners (or owners not flagged admin) get spurious FORBIDDEN instead of being authorized
matched_golden_ids: The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate points out the same permission logic bug: using && instead of || when checking isTeamAdminOrOwner, which incorrectly requires both admin and owner status rather than either one.

adjudication_records.issue_text: email-manager.ts:534-545 has inverted condition: if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email)) sends AttendeeScheduledEmail to newly added guests instead of AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, sending a booking confirmation email with ICS to people who never booked

adjudication.rationale: In `sendAddGuestsEmails` the condition is exactly `if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email))` then send `AttendeeScheduledEmail`, else send `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`. From the diff alone, this can reasonably be intentional: newly added guests get the full “scheduled/confirmation” email (with ICS), while existing attendees get a “guests added” notification. The finding asserts it is inverted and necessarily wrong, but the diff does not establish that intended behavior is to send `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail` to new guests instead.

adjudication_records.issue_text: email-manager.ts:529 / addGuests.handler.ts:155 passes raw guests to sendAddGuestsEmails instead of uniqueGuests, so organizer/team emails include duplicates and emails already present, diverging from the filtering intent

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler computes `uniqueGuests` by filtering out existing attendees / blacklisted emails, and uses that to create new attendee records. However it calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with the original unfiltered `guests` array. In `email-manager.ts`, `sendAddGuestsEmails` uses the passed `newGuests` list to decide which attendees get `AttendeeScheduledEmail` vs `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail` (`if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email)) ...`). Passing raw `guests` can incorrectly classify existing attendees (or otherwise filtered-out addresses) as “new guests” for email selection, diverging from the filtering intent. (The finding’s claim about organizer/team emails having duplicates is not supported, since organizer/team emails don’t use `newGuests`, but the core issue is real.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:140-149 builds EventManager from the calling user's credentials instead of the booking organizer's, so attendee-added guests fail to update the organizer's calendar event

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler explicitly allows an attendee to call the mutation (`isAttendee` check) but then constructs `EventManager` using the *calling* user (`...user` from `ctx.user`) and credentials from `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` (around lines ~140-149). Since the booking organizer is fetched separately (`organizer = await prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow(...)`) but their credentials are never used, an attendee-triggered add will attempt `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` with attendee credentials, which can fail to update the organizer’s calendar event (or update the wrong calendar). This mismatch is directly visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:82-84 returns validation error 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' for a filtering result, and silently drops partially filtered emails without user feedback, so user thinks all guests were added

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the server filters the requested `guests` into `uniqueGuests` by removing already-attending emails and blacklisted ones, but then (a) proceeds without returning which emails were actually added, so a request with some filtered-out emails still results in a generic success `{ message: "Guests added" }` and the UI toast `t("guests_added")`, and (b) if all emails are filtered out it throws `BAD_REQUEST` with message key `emails_must_be_unique_valid`, which is misleading because the failure can be due to being already attendees or blacklisted, not invalid/duplicate input. This matches the finding that partially filtered emails are silently dropped and the error message doesn’t reflect the actual filtering reason.

adjudication_records.issue_text: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS entries are lowercased but guest emails are compared unnormalized, allowing blacklist bypass via case variation

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` are normalized to lowercase (`.map((email) => email.toLowerCase())`), but incoming `guests` are compared without normalization: `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. Since `guest` may contain uppercase characters and `z.string().email()` does not lowercase, a blacklisted address can bypass the check via case variation (e.g., `Bad@Example.com`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicate-attendee check is case-sensitive, allowing an existing attendee to be re-added under different letter case

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, existing-attendee filtering uses strict equality `guest === attendee.email` when computing `uniqueGuests`, without normalizing case (e.g., lowercasing). Since emails can be provided with different letter case and Postgres/text comparisons are case-sensitive, an already-present attendee email could bypass this check and be re-added with different casing via `attendees.createMany`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && instead of ||, requiring user to be both admin AND owner rather than either

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, which requires the user to be both a team admin and a team owner. Given the variable name and the subsequent permission check `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee)`, this will incorrectly deny access to users who are only admin or only owner, so `||` is likely intended.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Booking lookup uses raw user-supplied id with no scoping in the query itself, relying on downstream checks that contain bugs

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the booking is fetched with `prisma.booking.findFirst({ where: { id: bookingId } ... })` using the user-supplied `bookingId` with no scoping to the current user/team in the query itself. The handler then distinguishes `NOT_FOUND` vs `FORBIDDEN`, which allows booking ID existence enumeration. Additionally, the downstream authorization check has a logic bug: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed with `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`, so a team admin who is not also an owner (or vice versa) will incorrectly fail the permission gate, demonstrating the “downstream checks that contain bugs” aspect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager is constructed with the requesting user's credentials instead of the booking organizer's, allowing attendees to trigger calendar writes with their own credentials

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler explicitly allows an attendee to call the mutation (`const isAttendee = ...` and the subsequent permission check). It then builds the calendar write context using the *requesting* user, not the booking organizer: `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);` and `const eventManager = new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] });` where `user` is `ctx.user`. That means an attendee can trigger `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` using their own connected calendar credentials rather than the organizer’s/booking owner’s, which can cause incorrect calendar updates or unauthorized writes relative to the booking organizer’s calendar integration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No upper bound on guests array, creating an unbounded email-amplification vector

adjudication.rationale: The new TRPC endpoint `addGuests` accepts `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.max()` or other bound (`packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts`). The handler then (a) writes all provided guests via `createMany` and (b) triggers external side effects: `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` and `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` (`addGuests.handler.ts`). With an unbounded `guests` array, an authorized caller can submit a very large list and cause large numbers of emails/calendar updates, creating an email-amplification/DoS vector.

adjudication_records.issue_text: sendAddGuestsEmails receives the raw input list instead of uniqueGuests, so filtered-out/blacklisted guests still receive the full booking email

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the DB update only creates `uniqueGuests` (filtered to exclude existing attendees and blacklisted emails), but the email dispatch uses the raw input list: `await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests);`. In `sendAddGuestsEmails`, the `newGuests` list is used to decide which template to send per attendee (`if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email)) ...`). If the caller included an email that was filtered out because it was already an attendee, that attendee still exists in `calendarEvent.attendees` and will incorrectly get the full `AttendeeScheduledEmail` again. (Blacklisted emails won’t be emailed since they aren’t in `attendees`, but the “filtered-out” case is a real behavioral defect.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: replyTo includes every attendee email including attacker-supplied guest addresses, enabling list-harvesting/reply-all amplification

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts`, the new email sets `replyTo: [this.calEvent.organizer.email, ...this.calEvent.attendees.map(({ email }) => email)]`, which includes all attendee emails. The attendee list is built in `addGuests.handler.ts` from `bookingAttendees.attendees` after creating new attendees from user-supplied `guests` emails, with no verification beyond basic email format/blacklist. This means attacker-supplied guest addresses will be placed into the Reply-To header, potentially exposing addresses and enabling reply-all amplification/list harvesting.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The entire feature (new tRPC mutation handler, two email templates, new UI component, and new form primitive) ships with no test code anywhere in the diff

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds substantial new behavior across UI (BookingListItem menu + new AddGuestsDialog + new MultiEmail form primitive), backend (new tRPC mutation addGuests with handler + schema), and email sending (sendAddGuestsEmails plus two new templates), but the diff contains no additions/changes to any test files (unit/integration/e2e). This is a concrete, diff-grounded gap for nontrivial logic (permissions checks, attendee updates, email branching) rather than a generic style nit.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Attendee createMany and updateCalendarAttendees/email sends run without a transaction, so a calendar update failure leaves committed attendee rows that were never added to the external calendar or emailed, with no rollback or compensating delete (addGuests.handler.ts:59-61)

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the DB is mutated first via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` and only afterwards the code calls `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` and then sends emails. There is no Prisma transaction or compensating rollback if `updateCalendarAttendees` throws (it is not wrapped in try/catch), so a calendar update failure would leave newly-created attendee rows committed while the external calendar (and subsequent email notifications) were not updated.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email failure error is swallowed at addGuests.handler.ts:166, making the partial-write failure mode silent

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, after updating DB attendees and calling `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees`, the code wraps `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` in a `try/catch` that only `console.log`s on failure and then still returns `{ message: "Guests added" }`. This diff-grounded behavior does swallow email-sending errors, creating a silent partial-success mode (guests added but notifications not sent) without surfacing the failure to the caller or error reporting.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dedupe check uses case-sensitive string compare while the blacklist lowercases, allowing a guest already attending as Foo@Example.com to be re-added as foo@example.com creating a duplicate Attendee row (addGuests.handler.ts:74-78)

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, deduping is done with strict equality against existing attendee emails: `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)`, and blacklist checking uses a lowercased blacklist array but compares against the raw `guest` string: `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. Since `guest` is not normalized (e.g., lowercased), `Foo@Example.com` and `foo@example.com` will be treated as different, allowing re-adding an attendee with different casing (and potentially bypassing the blacklist with casing), which can create duplicate attendee rows.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New attendee rows are created with name: "" and the organizer's timeZone/locale, bypassing normal booking flow values, causing malformed email headers (e.g. ' <>guest@x.com>') and organizer-tz-localized times in emails/ICS with no later backfill (addGuests.handler.ts:80-87)

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, new attendee records are created with `name: ""` and `timeZone/locale` taken from the organizer (guestsFullDetails mapping). This is then used to build attendee objects for emails/ICS (`name: attendee.name`, `timeZone: attendee.timeZone`, `language.locale: attendee.locale`). The email template `attendee-add-guests-email.ts` formats the recipient as `${this.attendee.name} <${this.attendee.email}>`, which with an empty name yields a malformed/undesirable header like ` <guest@x.com>`. The diff shows no subsequent enrichment/backfill of guest name/timezone/locale.

adjudication_records.issue_text: sendAddGuestsEmails is passed raw guests instead of uniqueGuests, so already-present or blacklisted emails are classified as new guests and receive a duplicate AttendeeScheduledEmail with a fresh ICS REQUEST instead of the 'guests added' email (addGuests.handler.ts:155)

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the server computes `uniqueGuests` by filtering out already-existing attendee emails and blacklisted emails, and only `uniqueGuests` are persisted via `createMany`. However it later calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` (raw input) instead of `uniqueGuests`. In email-manager.ts, `sendAddGuestsEmails` uses the provided `newGuests` array to decide which attendees get `AttendeeScheduledEmail` vs `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail` (`if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email)) ...`). If the input `guests` contains an email that is already an attendee, that attendee will be treated as a “new guest” and receive another `AttendeeScheduledEmail` (with a new ICS REQUEST) instead of the “guests added” notification. (Blacklisted emails won’t be emailed because they are not in `calendarEvent.attendees`.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...) conjunction at addGuests.handler.ts:36-38 requires caller to be both admin and owner; likely intended ||

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, which requires the caller to be both a team admin and a team owner. The variable name and subsequent permission gate (`if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) ... FORBIDDEN`) strongly imply intended semantics were “admin OR owner”; as written, legitimate admins (non-owners) or owners (non-admins) would be incorrectly blocked from adding guests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Team permission check uses && instead of || in addGuests.handler.ts:33-35, so team admins who are not owners are incorrectly denied with FORBIDDEN

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, which only returns true if the user is both an admin and an owner. The subsequent permission gate `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw FORBIDDEN` will therefore deny a team admin who is not also an owner, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow with booking.userId || 0 in addGuests.handler.ts:42-53 throws unhandled PrismaClientKnownRequestError when booking.userId is null or organizer deleted, leaking raw Prisma error as a 500 instead of a 4xx

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, after verifying `booking` exists, it loads the organizer via `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } ... })`. If `booking.userId` is `null/undefined` (the code explicitly guards with `|| 0`) or if the referenced organizer user no longer exists, `findFirstOrThrow` will throw (record-not-found) and there is no surrounding handling to convert this into a `TRPCError` (4xx). That would surface as an unhandled server error (500) rather than a controlled 4xx response, matching the finding's concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Database write commits before eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees with no transaction/rollback (addGuests.handler.ts:88-101,148), leaving permanent partial state where guests exist in DB but not on the calendar, and retries fail dedup validation

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the DB is updated first via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` (around lines 88-101), then `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` is executed later (~line 148) with no transaction/rollback. If `updateCalendarAttendees` throws, the mutation fails but the attendee rows are already permanently written, leaving guests in DB but not synced to the external calendar. On retry, `uniqueGuests` is computed by filtering out emails already present in `booking.attendees`, so it can become empty and the handler throws `BAD_REQUEST` (`emails_must_be_unique_valid`), preventing a retry from re-attempting calendar sync.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Catch block at addGuests.handler.ts:150-154 swallows email send errors and returns success message, so failed AddGuests emails are silently dropped with no logging of the error

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` call is wrapped in a `try/catch` and on failure it does not affect the response (`return { message: "Guests added" }`). The catch only does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` and does not log `err` details, so email delivery failures won’t be surfaced to the caller and are only weakly observable. The finding’s “no logging” wording is slightly off (there is a generic log), but the underlying concern (swallowed error + no error detail) is grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: isInvalidEmail in AddGuestsDialog.tsx is set to true but never reset when user edits input, so the error banner persists during a later successful mutation

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog.tsx`, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` on failed `safeParse` in `handleAdd`, but it is only reset in the Cancel button handler (`setIsInvalidEmail(false)`). It is not cleared when the user edits the `MultiEmail` inputs (only `setMultiEmailValue` is called) nor when validation succeeds / mutation starts or succeeds (the `onSuccess` resets `multiEmailValue` and closes the dialog but does not reset `isInvalidEmail`). Because the component remains mounted and state persists across open/close (`<Dialog open={isOpenDialog} ...>`), the error banner can persist during later valid submissions and/or when reopening the dialog.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Guest dedup and blacklist check is case-sensitive (addGuests.handler.ts:76-80), allowing case-variant emails to bypass duplicate and blacklist checks

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, blacklist values are normalized to lowercase (`split(...).map(email => email.toLowerCase())`), but incoming `guests` are compared without normalization: `guest === attendee.email` and `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. These strict, case-sensitive comparisons allow case-variant duplicates (e.g., `A@x.com` vs `a@x.com`) and allow bypassing the blacklist by changing email casing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: guests array schema (addGuests.schema.ts:5) has no .max() limit, allowing unbounded attendee creation and outbound email amplification including oversized reply-to headers

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts`, `guests` is defined as `z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.max(...)` (and the client-side schema in `AddGuestsDialog.tsx` also has no max). The handler (`addGuests.handler.ts`) will `createMany` attendees from this array and then `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`, which in turn sends emails per attendee and constructs an `replyTo` header including `...this.calEvent.attendees.map(({ email }) => email)` (`organizer-add-guests-email.ts`). With no bounded input size, a caller can submit a very large guests list, causing unbounded attendee creation and potentially excessive outbound email/header size.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager is constructed with the invoker's credentials (ctx.user) instead of the booking organizer's (addGuests.handler.ts:148), so non-organizer invocations fail or no-op on the organizer's calendar

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the calendar update is performed via `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`, but the `EventManager` is constructed with the *invoking* user context: `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user); const eventManager = new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] });` where `user` is `ctx.user`. Since this mutation explicitly allows non-organizers to invoke it (`isAttendee` / team admin/owner checks), those callers may not have the organizer’s calendar credentials, so updating the organizer’s calendar attendees can fail or no-op for non-organizer invocations.
